title: File 13 - the cold hard truth about board game development and publishing, by Tom Wham
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCTe19NTny4

Daniel (@dungeondive) digs out another game from the Best of Dragon Magazine Games box: Tom Wham's *File 13*, from Dragon #72 (April 1983), a satirical game about board game development itself. He calls Wham's games the kind of thing Mad Magazine might have published.

Up to four players compete to get two of their designs onto the sales chart as hot items. Each submission travels a flowchart of corporate peril: new submissions, the director of creative services, playtesters, a dozing product review board, the dreaded cost analysis, developers Myron Minuscule and Sam Semicolon, a loop of editors, art department and pre-press, then the printers, shipping (which Daniel says every crowdfunder will recognise) and finally the sales chart, from turkey to hot item. Failure sends your game to File 13, the wastebasket.

Movement is roll-and-move by destination table, and coloured cards provide the chaos. Green cards help you, red cards set rivals back ("company hires 35 new executives"), and blue cards are the only way to submit new designs. The joke titles parody real games, and Daniel notes some of the humour wouldn't fly today. He's puzzled by the recurring Peru jokes. His demo includes a lucky card sending Holy War straight from submission to the printers, where it promptly jams.

He expects Munchkin-style kingmaking and long endgames, but enjoyed it solo and suspects working designers will find it more painfully accurate than funny.

----

What's the most true-to-life part of game publishing that a satirical game like File 13 should poke fun at today?
